title: A Cartier divisor gives a supported Kummer map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an arbitrary integer $m\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. The coefficient sheaf $A_T$ and the finite-level Tate twist $A_T(1)$ are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] on the small pro-etale site; in particular this notation is not redefined by an etale tensor product. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor, a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and put $L=\mathcal O_T(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. There is a canonical morphism in the ordinary pro-etale derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]
$$c_{D,A}:i_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].$$
Its composite with $A_T\to i_*A_D$ is $c_{1,A}(L)$. Here $c_{1,A}$ is the etale Kummer boundary at any exponent $\ell^r$ killing $A$, extended to $A$ and pulled to the pro-etale site using [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], followed by the canonical projection-induced identification with the specified Tate twist. This definition is independent of $r$. For any morphism $h:T'\to T$ for which $D'=D\times_TT'$ is again Cartier, under the canonical supported-constant and Tate-twist comparisons, $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$. The construction is compatible with coefficient reductions $A_{E,b}\to A_{E,a}$ for $b\geq a\geq1$. No divisibility of $m$ by the ramification index is assumed. The etale-origin witness for the target is $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$; the same supported morphism on this etale witness gives the ordinary etale formulation used by etale callers.

proof.text: Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$ (one may take $r=m$: $\ell$ has positive integral valuation in $\mathcal O_E$, hence $\ell^m\in(\varpi_E^m)$). For steps 1-6 put $n=\ell^r$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and $B_{r,T}=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes^L_\Lambda A$; these are auxiliary etale objects, not a definition of $A(1)$. The dual ideal $L$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has a canonical section $s_D$, dual to $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$. On an open chart where $\mathcal I_D=(f_a)$ with $f_a$ a nonzerodivisor, the ideal is free on $f_a$, its dual is free on $e_a=f_a^{-1}$, and $s_D=f_ae_a$. On $V=T-D$, $f_a$ is a unit, so $s_D$ is a nowhere zero section and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_D:\mathcal O_V\cong L|_V$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, hence these formulas agree. The frame torsor $P_D=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L)$ of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] is therefore a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor with the specified section $\tau_D$ on $V$.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1-2: the Cartier line with its specified open trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to $(P_D,\tau_D)$ with $G=\mathbf G_m$. This gives a specified class $\alpha_D\in H^1(T,V;\mathbf G_m)$, independent of chart equations and refinements, whose forgotten-support image is the torsor class of $L$. For explicit changes of equations, $f'_a=u_af_a$ gives $e'_a=u_a^{-1}e_a$ and $f'_ae'_a=f_ae_a$; it is the same line bundle with the same section, not just an unspecified lift of its Picard class. The relative lemma supplies the comparison with derived sections; no assertion that an arbitrary ordinary Cech cover computes all derived cohomology is needed.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1-2: its relative cohomology class

proof.text: Since $n$ is invertible on $T$, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] supplies the short exact Kummer sequence $0\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf G_m\to0$. Apply its relative connecting map, provided by [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], to $\alpha_D$: $\beta_D=\delta_{T,V}(\alpha_D)\in H^2(T,V;\mu_n)$. The relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([L])$, exactly $c_{1,\Lambda}(L)$. Only the abelian-sheaf Kummer sequence is used: $\mathbf G_m$ is not a $\Lambda$-module and is never tensored over $\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: the relative Kummer boundary

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison] with $K=\mu_n[0]$, the identity of $T$ and the open inclusion $V\to T$. Its canonical coefficient-forgetting comparisons commute with restriction and identify every cohomology group, hence identify the two derived section complexes and their relative cones. In particular the relative abelian class $\beta_D$ defines a class in relative $\Lambda$-module cohomology. By [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], in degree two this is a morphism $c_{D,\Lambda}:i_*\Lambda_D\to\mu_{n,T}[2]$. The forgotten-support map is precomposition with $\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$: apply derived Hom to the open-closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact]; the first map into ordinary sections is induced by this quotient. Thus step 3 says $c_{D,\Lambda}\circ(\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D)=c_{1,\Lambda}(L)$. This is the support-Hom construction, without a purity assertion.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3 and paragraph 4, first sentence: module-valued supported Hom and forgetting support

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] along $\Lambda_T\to A_T$ to $c_{D,\Lambda}$. The target is $B_{r,T}[2]$. The source is canonically $i_*A_D$: the scalar-extension unit, followed by the sectionwise coefficient map, gives the comparison $(i_*\Lambda_D)\otimes^L_\Lambda A\to i_*A_D$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. At a geometric point on $D$ or off $D$, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives respectively $\Lambda$ or zero for the original supported sheaf, and $A$ or zero for the new one. By [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and [lem-kun-pullback-constant], the source stalks are $\Lambda\otimes^L_\Lambda A=A$ and zero, with comparison the identity. Exactness and conservativity of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to the cohomology sheaves of the cone, prove invertibility. Denote the resulting etale map by $\widetilde c_{D,r,A}$. The restriction map becomes $A_T\to i_*A_D$ by the same stalk calculation, so its composite is the extended Kummer boundary. No flatness of $A$ over $\Lambda$ is used.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: derived scalar extension and its supported source

proof.text: Let $h:T'\to T$ with $D'=T'\times_TD$ Cartier. Pull back the equations of step 1. Each $f'_a=h^*f_a$ generates the ideal of $D'$ and is a nonzerodivisor, by the Cartier hypothesis. The dual basis $e'_a=(f'_a)^{-1}$ satisfies $e'_b=h^*(f_a/f_b)e'_a$ and $s_{D'}=f'_ae'_a$. These formulas identify $(h^*L,h^*s_D)$ with $(\mathcal O_{T'}(D'),s_{D'})$, including their trivializations off $D'$. On frame torsors use the coefficient map $h^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$ sending a unit to its pullback. By [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] the relative class becomes $\alpha_{D'}$. The maps of Kummer sequences commute since $h^*(u^n)=h^*(u)^n$, so their relative boundaries carry $\beta_D$ to $\beta_{D'}$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: pullback of the Cartier pair and its relative boundary

proof.text: By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] the map $h^{-1}\mu_{n,T}\to\mu_{n,T'}$ is an isomorphism, with identity and composition compatibility. The canonical closed-support exchange $h^{-1}i_*\Lambda_D\to i'_*\Lambda_{D'}$ is an isomorphism: using [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula, lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback, lem-kun-pullback-constant], its geometric stalk is the identity of $\Lambda$ over $D'$ and the identity of zero elsewhere; apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The support-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] respects this exchange: compute it by applying derived Hom to the open-closed sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact]; the pullback and adjunction maps send its quotient to the supported quotient just calculated and its restriction map to restriction on $T'\setminus D'$. Thus its cone map is the relative pullback map used in step 6. The coefficient-forgetting comparison is compatible with those restriction maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison]. Hence $h^{-1}c_{D,\Lambda}=c_{D',\Lambda}$. By [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and [lem-kun-pullback-constant], scalar extension to $A$ commutes with $h^{-1}$. This gives $h^{-1}\widetilde c_{D,r,A}=\widetilde c_{D',r,A}$, including forgetting support.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: supported etale base change before scalar extension

proof.text: The etale sheaf $\mu_{\ell^r}$ is flat of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], applied to $A=\Lambda$. It is K-flat in degree zero by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], so $B_{r,T}=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_\Lambda A$ in degree zero. Put $M=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$. Tensor associativity in the original definition [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] gives $A_T(1)=M\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}A_T$. Since $\ell^rA=0$, this equals $(M/\ell^rM)\otimes_{\Lambda_T}A_T$. Both $M/\ell^rM$ and $M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}}\Lambda_T$ are the cokernel of $\ell^r:M\to M$. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] therefore identifies them with $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}$ by the inverse-limit projection $p_r$. This proves the required twist comparison for every $m$, without $e\mid m$. The comparison $\nu_T^*\mu_{\ell^r}^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mu_{\ell^r}^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an isomorphism: on a root-trivializing etale cover of clause (1) it sends the chosen generator to that same generator. Exact comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] now give $q_{r,T}:\nu_T^*B_{r,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$. Its inverse sends $x\otimes a$ to $p_r(x)\otimes a$.

source.place: Proof, final scalar-extension sentence: comparison with the original pro-etale Tate twist

proof.text: Put $j:T\setminus D\hookrightarrow T$. On every affine chart where the Cartier ideal is generated by $f$, the complement is the quasi-compact principal open $D(f)$; quasi-compactness is local on the target, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to etale $A_T$ and pull the sequence to the pro-etale site using [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] its first arrow identifies with $j_!A_{T\setminus D}\to A_T$, with the usual counit (the canonical comparison is its adjunction mate). By [lem-sf-proetale-open-closed-sequence] the cokernel of that counit is $i_*A_D$, and its quotient map is the adjunction unit. The resulting quotient isomorphism $a_T:\nu_T^*(i_*^{\mathrm{et}}A_D)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*^{\mathrm{proet}}A_D$ consequently identifies the two supported restriction maps. This checks the quasi-compactness hypothesis needed on the pro-etale side.

source.place: Proof, final scalar-extension sentence: transport of the supported constant source

proof.text: Using [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], define $c_{D,A}=q_{r,T}[2]\circ\nu_T^*(\widetilde c_{D,r,A})\circ a_T^{-1}$. Precomposition with $A_T\to i_*A_D$ becomes $q_{r,T}[2]\circ\nu_T^*(c_{1,r,A}(L))$ by steps 5 and 9. This is precisely the specified Kummer definition of $c_{1,A}(L)$. The etale-origin witness is $B_{r,T}$ and the etale supported morphism producing it is $\widetilde c_{D,r,A}$.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: definition of the pro-etale morphism from its etale witness

proof.text: For $s\geq r$, write $R_s=\mathbf Z/\ell^s$ and $R_r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. There is a diagram of Kummer sequences from exponent $\ell^s$ to exponent $\ell^r$, with middle map $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{s-r}}$, right map the identity, and kernel map $p_{s,r}:\mu_{\ell^s}\to\mu_{\ell^r}$ given by that power. By [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] it sends $\beta_{D,s}$ to $\beta_{D,r}$. The module comparison and support-Hom construction of step 4 therefore identify $p_{s,r}[2]c_{D,R_s}$ with $c_{D,R_r}$ precomposed with $i_*R_{s,D}\to i_*R_{r,D}$, in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R_s)$ after restriction of scalars. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], extension of $p_{s,r}$ to $R_r$ identifies the two finite Tate lines. The supported source extends to $i_*R_{r,D}$ by step 5. The adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] thus turns this equality into equality after extension to $R_r$. Successive extension to $A$ agrees with direct extension: on a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms, [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] allows both to be computed by $(P\otimes_{R_s}R_r)\otimes_{R_r}A\cong P\otimes_{R_s}A$. Finally $p_r=p_{s,r}p_s$ by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], so the formula for $q$ in step 8 commutes with this comparison. Substitution in step 10 proves independence of $r$; compare arbitrary allowed exponents through their maximum.

source.place: Proof, final scalar-extension sentence: independence of the auxiliary Kummer exponent

proof.text: For $b\geq a\geq1$, choose one $r$ killing both $A_{E,b}$ and $A_{E,a}$. Use [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]: a K-flat representative $P$ with flat terms computes the composite coefficient extension by $(P\otimes_\Lambda A_{E,b})\otimes_{A_{E,b}}A_{E,a}\cong P\otimes_\Lambda A_{E,a}$. This sends the extended supported morphism at $b$ to that at $a$. The source comparisons of step 5 send $1\otimes b$ to $\bar b$, and the target comparisons of step 8 send $x\otimes b$ to $p_r(x)\otimes b$ before reduction and to $p_r(x)\otimes\bar b$ after it. Thus the $q$ maps commute with reduction. Exact site pullback commutes with these ordinary tensor presentations by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]; the supported quotient maps of step 9 commute as well. Hence coefficient extension carries $c_{D,A_{E,b}}$ to $c_{D,A_{E,a}}$. Three successive reductions have the same map on pure tensors, giving coherence.

source.place: Proof, final scalar-extension sentence: compatibility with all finite coefficient reductions

proof.text: For a Cartier-preserving $h:T'\to T$, the base-change functors defining [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and the inclusion defining [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] commute on underlying schemes and arrows. Their adjunctions give $h^{-1}\nu_T^*\cong\nu_{T'}^*h^{-1}$; the composition and tensor compatibilities are those of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Finite constant rings pull back canonically by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. The maps $a_T$ of step 9 commute with $h$ because they are the quotient maps of the same open-extension counit, using [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]; therefore the etale supported-source exchange of step 7 supplies the supported-constant comparison on the pro-etale site. The $q$ maps commute too: $h^*(u^{\ell^{s-r}})=h^*(u)^{\ell^{s-r}}$ makes the inverse-limit projections commute with the natural map $h^{-1}M_T\to M_{T'}$, and step 8's formula is $x\otimes a\mapsto p_r(x)\otimes a$. On finite root-trivializing covers, [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies this with the identity of the constant $A$-line, so it is the Tate-twist comparison isomorphism. Substitute these comparisons and the step-7 equality into step 10 to obtain $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$. Identity and composite pullbacks agree because every quotient, root projection and pure-tensor map used here does, as do the cited site-composition comparisons.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: transport of Cartier base change through the original Tate-twist comparison

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
There is a natural morphism in the ordinary derived category

$$
c_D:i_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].
$$

Its image after forgetting support is
$c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$. For any base change under which
the pullback divisor remains Cartier, the map pulls back to
the corresponding map for that divisor.

proof.text:
First take coefficients $\mathbf Z/n$. Write
$v:T-D\hookrightarrow T$. The line bundle
$\mathcal O_T(D)$, together with its canonical trivialization
on $T-D$, defines an element of

$$
H^1\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,\mathbf G_m)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T-D,\mathbf G_m))[-1]\bigr).
$$

For completeness, choose local equations $f_a$ of $D$.
The transition units $f_a/f_b$ define the line bundle,
and the invertible functions $f_a$ on the complement give
its specified trivialization. The equality
$(f_a/f_b)(f_b/f_c)=f_a/f_c$ is the cocycle equation,
and restriction of the transition units is the coboundary of
these trivializing functions. These two assertions are exactly
the cocycle equation in the displayed relative cone. Replacing
$f_a$ by a unit times $f_a$ changes that cocycle by a
coboundary. Refining the covering preserves its class. One may
compute the cone on an injective resolution, or on etale
hypercovers refining this covering; the description gives the
same class in either computation.

Apply the connecting map of the Kummer sequence
[lem-amb-kummer-any-base] to this relative class. It gives
$c_D\in H_D^2(T,\mu_n)$. Forgetting the relative
trivialization sends it to the Kummer boundary of the line
bundle, namely its first Chern class. The support triangle in
[lem-amb-closed-support-hom] identifies

$$
H_D^2(T,\mu_n)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,\mathbf Z/n)}
(i_*\mathbf Z/n,\mu_n[2]).
$$

This identification uses the sheaf-level adjunction between
$i_*$ and sections supported on $D$, derived by
injective resolutions; it does not assert a purity isomorphism.
All the cone maps and Kummer boundaries commute with pullback
of the pair and its trivialized line bundle. This proves the
asserted base-change compatibility whenever the pulled-back
pair is again the Cartier pair of
[def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor].
Finally apply derived scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/n$
to $A$. Its source is $i_*A_D$, as seen on stalks,
and its target is $A_T(1)[2]$ by
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. No flatness of $A$ over
$\mathbf Z/n$ is needed.
